newsitem.title: UK: Cargill says works with IPE on delivery problems.
newsitem.headline: Cargill says works with IPE on delivery problems.

text.p: Trading house Cargill said on Tuesday it was working with the International Petroleum Exchange (IPE) and all parties to the November IPE gas oil contract to resolve what it called continuing problems of delivery.
Cargill, the main long on the contract, added in a statement from its Minneapolis headquarters in the United States that it was confident that such issues would be resolved promptly through the IPE.
"Cargill is working with IPE authorities and all parties to the November IPE contract to try to resolve the continuing problems regarding delivery under this contract," the statement said.
"We remain confident that these issues will be resolved promptly through the IPE and IPE enforcement system."
Monte Carlo-based AIC, the main short on the contract, alleged on Friday that Cargill was behind on its nominations for the second five-day delivery window that expired at midnight on Monday.
AIC earlier last week also said Cargill had failed to lift the required volume of gas oil in the first five-day period of the November 16-30 delivery window.

Cargill, in an apparent response to that charge, said on Thursday there had been some problems in the first five-day delivery period but it hoped to resolve these through IPE channels. It added it was confident the IPE would resolve any dispute in a prompt and just manner.

Cargill is due to take delivery of a total of at least 627,800 tonnes, to be lifted in three five-day periods, November 16-20, November 21-25 and November 26-30. The delivery was a record high 865,1000 tonnes.
